html:
Small brass weights used by the Akan of Ghana and Ivory Coast to weigh gold dust, which was their money, from about the 15th century to the early 20th century.

Cast by the lost-wax method, they range from geometric shapes to tiny figures of people, animals, tools and scenes, many of which stand for proverbs. Every trader and chief kept a set with scales and spoons. The weights follow Islamic and Portuguese units, a sign of the trade links north through Bono and south to Elmina. Tens of thousands survive, and they are among the best-known objects of West African art. See also Asante.
sum: Small brass weights used by the Akan of Ghana and Ivory Coast to weigh gold dust, which was their money, from about the 15th century to the early 20th century.
